narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Dry conditions persist through tonight and into tomorrow, though elevated convective instability brings a potential for isolated evening thunder peaking around 19:00 EAT. Numerical models disagree significantly on CAPE intensity tonight, ranging from minimal values on GFS (110 J/kg) to near 2,830 J/kg on Best Match.

## Today's Forecast
With evening underway, daytime warmth is giving way to moderate nighttime temperatures settling near 18°C / 64°F under partly cloudy skies. Southwesterly winds at 12 to 22 km/h (6 to 12 kt) will gradually ease after midnight. Tomorrow (Friday) brings hot conditions with daytime highs reaching 33°C to 35°C / 91°F to 95°F (Kenya Met predicts 32°C / 90°F). UV exposure will reach Very High levels around midday (peak UV 9.1), requiring sun protection between 10:00 and 15:00 EAT. While surface models forecast 0.0 mm of precipitation through tomorrow, elevated CAPE spikes between 18:00 and 22:00 EAT tonight, creating a risk for localized dry lightning and thunder. Ground air quality sensors are currently stale (most recent reading: Dunga Beach US AQI 69, taken 3 hours ago). CAMS model guidance indicates Moderate air quality with US AQI between 76 and 80.

## Extended Outlook
Days 1-3 (Aug 28–30): High confidence in dry weather through the weekend. Daytime high temperatures will hold between 33°C and 35°C (91°F–95°F), with overnight minimums around 17°C to 19°C (63°F–66°F). Days 4-7 (Aug 31–Sep 3): Lower confidence towards mid-next week. ECMWF and Best Match indicate rain returning by Sept 2–3 (0.2 to 2.8 mm) alongside cooler daytime highs near 29°C to 31°C (84°F–88°F), whereas GFS maintains dry, hot weather up to 35°C (95°F).

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No widespread flooding or heavy rainfall hazards are anticipated. Midday UV index reaching 9.1 tomorrow presents a high sunburn risk. High convective energy (CAPE peaking at 2,830 J/kg around 19:00 EAT) introduces a hazard of isolated dry lightning, sudden wind squalls, and thunder tonight despite dry surface forecasts.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Evening winds across the lake will blow from the SW/W at 18 to 25 km/h (10 to 14 kt) with gusts reaching 35 to 41 km/h (19 to 22 kt), turning easterly by dawn. High evening CAPE over open water creates a risk of sudden convective wind squalls and isolated thunder between 18:00 and 22:00 EAT.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1006 hPa) and highest toward the south (1020 hPa) — a 14 hPa spread, a strong large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is near-steady at 1012.8 hPa, with pressure also falling toward the north. Across the Nyanza Basin, regional MSLP points display a mild south-to-north gradient ranging from 1012.8 hPa near Kisumu to 1015.5 hPa at southern inland elevated stations, maintaining broad surface stability. Ground AQI reporting is currently stale across all local stations: Kisumu Airport (AQI 64, PM2.5 64.0 µg/m³), Ochieng' Avenue (AQI 59, PM2.5 59.0 µg/m³), and Dunga Beach (AQI 69, PM2.5 69.0 µg/m³, currently worst station), all 3 hours old. Air quality assessment therefore relies primarily on CAMS model guidance (US AQI 76–80).

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Per long-run review findings across 16 verified checks, Best Match holds the strongest Day+0 rain tracking record (88%), while GFS systematically overestimates surface wind speeds by over 18 km/h. ICON delivers strong daytime high accuracy (+0.3°C error) but exhibits a systematic overnight cold bias (-2.5°C), whereas UKMO shows a nocturnal warm bias (+1.1°C to +1.4°C). Kenya Met explicitly calls for a high of 32.0°C and a low of 16.0°C tomorrow with sunny intervals; we lean slightly warmer (33°C–35°C) in line with numerical consensus and verified recent model performance. Long-run review findings at Day+0 and Day+3 establish usable ranking and bias conclusions, but sample size at Day+7 is not yet sufficient to rank models conclusively.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Best Match holds the strongest Day+0 rain tracking record (88%), while GFS consistently overestimates surface wind speeds by 18-20 km/h. ICON provides excellent daytime high accuracy (+0.3°C) but exhibits an overnight cold bias (-2.5°C).
